title: Infrastructure Playbook: GPU Fleet, Capacity, Cloud Accounts, IaC & CI/CD (Ops Guide)
author: Jordan Lee
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational standards for the GPU fleet and capacity planning, cloud accounts and VPC networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD and build pipelines, and the most common infra runbooks used by on-call and platform teams. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and releng owners.

Scope

- GPU fleet provisioning and lifecycle (compute pools, autoscaling, preemptible vs dedicated)
- Capacity planning and buffer policy for production and staging
- Cloud account structure, VPC patterns, and cross-account networking (Transit/Gateway)
- Terraform/IaC module conventions and release process
- CI/CD build and deploy pipeline patterns for infra modules and runtime services
- Runbooks for common operational procedures (scale up/down, node replacement, outage recovery)

Ownership & Slack channels

- Primary owner: eng-infra (Platform & GPU Fleet subteam)
- Secondary owners: eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime (for runtime-level tuning)
- Slack channels: #infra-gpu-fleet, #infra-networking, #infra-deploys

GPU Fleet & Capacity Policy

Goals and SLOs

- SLO: GPU allocation latency <= 60s (p50) for elastic requests; p99 <= 300s for cold-starts.
- SLO: Node readiness after provisioning <= 300s (p95).
- Operational target: maintain 20% spare capacity above committed load for production-stage clusters.

Pool types and recommended use

- dedicated-reserved: long-lived nodes for Dedicated customers and pinned workloads. Autoscale disabled, manual capacity changes through capacity-controller.
- elastic-preemptible: cheap/spot instances for best-effort workloads and batch jobs; configured with graceful eviction and checkpointing.
- burst-pool: small set (~10% of prod reserved) held warm for sudden bursts and used by latency-sensitive hosted API under high load.

Capacity thresholds and alerts (examples)

- Alert: GPU_utilization > 85% (cluster) for 15m -> Pager to oncall if sustained and pending pods > 10.
- Alert: Pending_pods > 15 across serving namespace for 10m -> SEV-2.
- Daily cadence: capacity report generated at 02:00 UTC showing 7/30/90 day trends.

Scaling & Buffering rules

1) Maintain 20% buffer on production clusters: target_capacity = forecasted_peak * 1.2
2) Maintain a warm burst pool = max(1, ceil(0.1 * reserved_capacity)) GPUs
3) For preemptible-only workloads, the scheduler must support checkpointing and a minimum retry delay of 30s

Cloud Accounts & Networking

Account topology

- Organization root -> billing accounts per cloud (aws-account-billing)
- Environment accounts: prod, staging, dev, test, analytics, shared-services
- Customer-dedicated accounts for Private deployments are managed separately under private-accounts/ with restricted access.

VPC & connectivity patterns

- Standard VPC per account with 3 AZ subnets (public/priv/lambda).
- Transit connectivity: use Transit Gateway (AWS) or Cloud Router (GCP) for cross-account networking.
- Egress: centralized NAT gateway in shared-services with egress firewall rules.
- Peering: service-specific peering only by exception; prefer Transit Gateway for scale.

Network controls and security

- All management plane services (fleet-manager, capacity-controller) run in private subnets with restricted SGs.
- Bastion access via SSO-backed jumpbox; no direct external SSH allowed.
- VPC Flow logs must be enabled for prod and retained 90 days.

Terraform / IaC Modules & Conventions

Repository structure

- infra-iac (mono-repo) with these top-level modules:
  - modules/vpc
  - modules/gpu-cluster
  - modules/iam
  - modules/monitoring
  - modules/terraform-backend

Module conventions

- Modules must be small, composable, and documented. Public variables must have descriptions.
- Naming convention: module/resource names use kebab-case and are prefixable by account/env, e.g. redwood-prod-gpu-cluster.
- Default tags: {owner = "infra-gpu", cost_center = "platform", environment = "${var.env}"}.

State management

- Remote state in S3 with state locking via DynamoDB (AWS). Backend module lives at modules/terraform-backend.
- State write access limited to CI service account and trusted engineers.

Change process and PR checklist

1) Open PR against infra-iac with a clear summary of intent and risk.
2) Run terraform plan in CI and post plan output to PR.
3) Verify plan reviewer from eng-infra and eng-sre; at least one approver with infra-iac reviewer role.
4) Ensure no destructive changes to prod without runbook and a scheduled maintenance window.

PR checklist (short):
- [ ] Variables documented
- [ ] No hard-coded secrets (use vault/KMS)
- [ ] Plan reviewed and acceptable
- [ ] Rollback plan or restore point identified for prod-impacting changes

CI/CD & Build Pipelines

Pipeline patterns

- Infra modules: Buildkite pipeline infra-iac-pipeline runs terraform fmt/check, terragrunt plan, unit tests, and plan comment. Manual promote step required to apply to prod.
- Runtime/service images: buildkite/redwood-build publishes images to ECR/GCR, runs image-scan, and promotes to staging. Deployment controlled by redwood-deploy-bot.
- Canary & rollbacks: use canary deployments with automatic rollback on error rate > 2% in 5m or p50 latency regression > 100ms.

Secrets and credentials

- CI uses short-lived OIDC tokens for cloud operations where possible. Long-lived service accounts are stored in KMS and referenced by CI with least privilege.

Key CI commands (examples)

- Format & validate: terraform fmt -check && terraform validate
- Plan (example): buildkite-agent pipeline upload .buildkite/infra-plan.yml

- Apply (manual gated): terraform apply -auto-approve 

Runbooks & Operational Procedures

Common runbooks (high level)

1) Scale up GPU capacity (oncall -> SRE/Infra)
   - When to run: GPU_utilization alert triggered OR pending_pods > 10 for 10m.
   - Steps:
     1. Confirm alert in Grafana and check cluster metrics.
     2. Verify current reserved vs elastic pools: kubectl get nodes -l poolType --sort-by=.metadata.name
     3. For immediate capacity: trigger capacity-controller scale-up: 
        ./tools/capacity-controller scale --env prod --pool elastic-preemptible --count +8
     4. Monitor node readiness: kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node -l gpu=true --timeout=600s
     5. If nodes fail to become Ready, rollback: 
        ./tools/capacity-controller scale --env prod --pool elastic-preemptible --count -8
     6. Post-incident: open postmortem if capacity gap > 5% or user-facing impact.

2) Replace unhealthy GPU node
   - Steps:
     1. cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
     2. drain with DaemonSet considerations: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
     3. deprovision via node pool tool: ./tools/gpu-provisioner deprovision --node <node>
     4. reprovision using same AZ and instance type via terraform apply on module with count change or call capacity-controller.

3) Emergency rollback of infra module change (prod)
   - Steps:
     1. Revert PR in infra-iac and re-run CI plan for prod.
     2. If immediate revert required, notify stakeholders, schedule 15-min maintenance window, and run terraform apply with previous state file snapshot.
     3. Validate critical systems (fleet-manager, capacity-controller, API endpoints) are healthy.

Operational playbooks & run cadence

- Weekly: infra runbook review in platform sync.
- Monthly: capacity forecast review with product/finance to update reserved commitments.
- Quarterly: IaC audit (module drift, unused resources) and clean-up plan.

Appendix: Common commands & Templates

- Check pending pods: kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n serving | wc -l
- Node readiness: kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide
- Terraform apply (example): 
  cd infra-iac/environments/prod/gpu-cluster && terraform init && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform apply "plan.tfplan"

Terraform module example header (modules/gpu-cluster/main.tf):

```
variable "env" { description = "Environment name" type = string }
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_asg" {
  name_prefix = "${var.env}-gpu-asg-"
  desired_capacity = var.desired_capacity
  ...
}
```
